$comment: Failure-mode playground. The diagram is a generic LLM-pipeline topology (client → proxy → service → gateway → model endpoints); node cards describe patterns, not any specific deployment.

card.job: Opens a server-streaming RPC and renders progress while a multi-minute job runs.
card.guards: Cancelling from here must actually stop work upstream, not just stop listening.
card.tradeoff: Streaming progress is more complex than request/response, but a 6-minute spinner with no feedback is a support ticket.

card.job: TLS termination, routing, and the idle timeout that protects the fleet from abandoned connections.
card.guards: Connections that nobody is reading any more.
card.tradeoff: Its timeout is a fleet-wide setting owned by another team. Rather than negotiate a special case, the service emits heartbeats and works under the default.

card.job: Runs the document pipeline: classify, triage, extract per page, batched enrichment, feasibility, translation. Streams progress back.
card.guards: Overload (bounded admission with runtime-adjustable limits), proxy idle kills (queue heartbeats), leaked work on cancel (structured concurrency), malformed model output (repair at every parse site).
card.tradeoff: Bounded admission means some requests wait in a queue instead of starting immediately. Waiting with a heartbeat beats starting and timing out.

card.job: One OpenAI-compatible door for every service: model aliases, parameter normalisation per model family, load balancing across endpoints, per-call cost attribution.
card.guards: A single slow or failing endpoint taking the platform down (circuit breaker with cooldown and probation), flat timeouts that are wrong for every prompt size (token-aware adaptive timeout), unbounded fan-in (admission with explicit backpressure).
card.tradeoff: Another hop and another service to run. In exchange, retries, fallbacks and cost accounting live in one tested place instead of in every caller.

card.job: A hosted model deployment behind a quota.
card.guards: Nothing — it is the thing everything else guards against.
card.tradeoff: Multiple endpoints cost more to configure and monitor; a single one is a single point of failure with a rate limit.

card.job: Same model, different region and quota.
card.guards: Regional incidents and per-endpoint rate limits.
card.tradeoff: Cross-region latency is slightly higher; it is only used when least-in-flight routing prefers it.

card.job: Third endpoint; normally receives the least traffic.
card.tradeoff: Idle capacity most of the time. During an incident it is the difference between degraded and down.

edges.label: gRPC
edges.flow: Request: document reference, processing options, deadline
Response stream: progress frames, heartbeats, final result
Forwarded stream with cancellation propagated as context cancel
Progress frames every stage; heartbeat frames every 15 s while idle

edges.label: LLM
edges.flow: Batched prompts with JSON schema, model alias, token budget
Parsed completion, token usage, attempt count, cost attribution
HTTPS request to endpoint A with adaptive timeout
HTTPS request to endpoint B (fallback / least-in-flight)
HTTPS request to endpoint C (last resort)

scenarios.label: Happy path
scenarios.description: A 96-page document, no surprises. Use this as the baseline before injecting anything.

scenarios.label: Malformed model output
scenarios.description: The model hits its output limit and returns truncated JSON for a batch of twelve items.
scenarios.guard: Repair at every parse site, partial-batch acceptance, and a narrower retry — nothing is dropped silently.

scenarios.label: Endpoint timeout
scenarios.description: One endpoint stops producing tokens. A flat 30-second timeout would either fire too early on big prompts or too late on small ones.
scenarios.guard: Token-aware adaptive timeout, per-failure-class cooldown, retry on the next least-loaded endpoint.

scenarios.label: Client cancels
scenarios.description: The user closes the tab two minutes into a job. Everything in flight must stop and release its slot.
scenarios.guard: End-to-end cancellation: context cancel → task cancel → upstream abort → admission slot freed.

scenarios.label: Provider outage
scenarios.description: Two of three endpoints return 503 at the same time.
scenarios.guard: Circuit breaker with open → half-open → probation states and anti-flap, plus backpressure to the caller.

scenarios.label: Proxy idle timeout
scenarios.description: Dense pages take 40 seconds each; the proxy closes any stream that is silent for 60 seconds.
scenarios.guard: Queue heartbeats emitted on a timer, independent of model output.
